chronic heat stress, chronic ethanol consumption and chronic heat stress combined with chronic ethanol consumption all produced mild hypertension in the rat.
chronic ethanol consumption and chronic stress, when combined, produced a more severe form of hypertension than that produced by the two treatments when applied separately.
chronic stress and chronic ethanol ingestion, when combined, produce more severe hypertension than that observed in animals receiving each treatment alone.

the effects of chronic heat stress and ethanol consumption on cardiovascular function in rats.
the interaction between chronic alcohol consumption and physical stress in the development of hypertension.
the interaction between chronic alcohol intake and physical stress.

the combined treatment of heat stress and chronic alcohol consumption in rats produced additive effects in the elevation of arterial blood pressure.
chronic ethanol consumption and chronic stress, when combined, produce additive effects on the blood pressure of rats and are associated with increased sympathetic tone and mortality.
the interaction of chronic ethanol consumption and heat stress in the rat results in a greater degree of hypertension than either treatment alone.

chronic heat stress and chronic alcohol consumption each produced mild increases in blood pressure in rats and that when combined, the two produced a more pronounced increase in blood pressure than either treatment alone.
chronic ethanol consumption and heat stress, when combined, produce more severe hypertension than either stress or ethanol alone.

stress can exacerbate the effects of chronic ethanol consumption on the cardiovascular system.

the combination of stress and ethanol can be a potent risk factor for the development of hypertension in humans.
